name: Dashboards and Product UI Rulebook
summary: Dashboards, admin panels, tools and settings: shell, data, charts, tables and states.
check: Load realistic data at small, normal and huge volumes.
Force one widget to fail; the rest keeps working.

rules.title: The task before the look
rules.text: Someone who uses tools like this should know where everything is before they notice the style. Style comes through type, palette, density and one signature move, never through a strange layout or invented controls.

rules.title: A standard shell
rules.text: Side navigation (collapsible) or top bar, a page header with title and primary action, then the work area. Breadcrumbs for deep hierarchies, a command menu for power users.

rules.title: A second neutral for chrome
rules.text: Sidebar and toolbars sit on a slightly different neutral than the content surface, so structure is visible without borders everywhere.

rules.title: Density with a choice
rules.text: Comfortable by default, compact available where people scan many rows. Compact means tighter spacing, not smaller type below `TY-06`.

rules.title: Lead with the question
rules.text: The first thing on a dashboard answers the user's main question ("Are we on track this month?"), not a wall of equal KPI tiles.

rules.title: Numbers with context
rules.text: Every headline number shows its unit, its period and a comparison (vs last period, vs target) and, when it changes over time, a small trend line with the change marked.

rules.title: Charts that fit the question
rules.text: Line for change over time, bar for comparison, stacked bar for parts of a whole over time, table for exact values. No pie charts with more than about five slices, no 3D charts, no dual axes without labels.

rules.title: Honest charts
rules.text: Bar charts start at zero, axes are labelled with units, series are labelled directly where possible, and colour is never the only key (`CL-10`). Follow `dataviz` guidance for palettes.

rules.title: Real tables
rules.text: Sticky header, sortable columns with a visible sort state, right-aligned tabular numbers (`DC-18`), left-aligned text, row hover, selection with bulk actions, pagination or virtualisation for long lists (`PF-10`).

rules.title: Filters over what they filter
rules.text: Filters sit above or beside the data they scope, show what is active, and can be cleared in one action. The URL keeps filter state so views can be shared.

rules.title: Skeletons, not spinners in content
rules.text: Loading tables and charts show their own shape (`ST-02`).

rules.title: Empty states teach
rules.text: A new account's empty dashboard explains what will appear and offers the first action, with sample data clearly labelled as sample if shown (`ST-01`).

rules.title: Partial failure
rules.text: One failed widget shows its own error and retry; the rest of the dashboard keeps working.

rules.title: Status colours only for status
rules.text: Red for critical, amber for warning, green for success, blue for information, each with an icon or label. Inactive items are not shown in full-saturation colours.

rules.title: Fast transitions
rules.text: 150–250 ms for UI changes, no page-load choreography, no decorative motion (`MO-02`).

rules.title: Inline over modal
rules.text: Edit in place or in a side panel; keep context. Modals only for short focused tasks (`IX-07`).

rules.title: Respect power users
rules.text: Keyboard navigation in tables, shortcuts for frequent actions, bulk operations, saved views.

rules.title: Realistic demo data
rules.text: Mockups and empty-account demos use plausible names, values and units, with one interesting state visible (an alert, a degraded service), never tiles of random numbers (`SL-20`).

rules.title: Data freshness and time zone
rules.text: Every dashboard shows when the data was last updated and which time zone it uses.

rules.title: Compact numbers with exact values on demand
rules.text: Large numbers are shortened (48.2k) in tiles and charts, with the exact value in a tooltip or table.

rules.title: Export and share
rules.text: Tables and charts that people report from can be exported (CSV) and the current view shared by URL.

rules.title: Accessible charts
rules.text: Every chart has a text summary and a data table alternative; series are distinguishable without colour.

rules.title: Gauges and speedometers
rules.text: No dials, gauges or speedometer charts. A number with a target and a bar says the same thing in a fraction of the space.

rules.title: Rainbow palettes in charts
rules.text: No rainbow or random colours for data. Use a sequential palette for ordered values and a small categorical palette for categories.

rules.title: A wall of KPIs
rules.text: No more than about four to six headline numbers above the fold. Everything else is one click away.

rules.title: Auto-refresh that moves content
rules.text: Live updates never shift what the user is reading or clicking. Show "3 new items" and let people load them.
